root.label: Parallel algorithms
root.note: An execution policy grants the library permission to parallelize; your callbacks must tolerate it.

children.label: The four policies
children.note: seq, par and par_unseq since C++17; unseq since C++20, all in <execution>.

children.label: seq
children.note: Calling thread only; invocations do not overlap but their order is unspecified.

children.label: par
children.note: Calling or library threads; invocations on one thread never overlap.

children.label: par_unseq
children.note: Any threads, and invocations may be interleaved within one thread.

children.label: unseq
children.note: Calling thread only, but invocations may be interleaved for vectorization.

children.label: Element access functions
children.note: Iterator operations, required element operations and your function objects.

children.label: Data races
children.note: The library adds no synchronization; races between invocations are UB.

children.label: Locks under par
children.note: Allowed, but never wait for another invocation that may not have started.

children.label: Vectorization-unsafe
children.note: Mutex locking is forbidden under par_unseq and unseq; allocation is exempt.

children.label: Exceptions
children.note: Policy overloads change error handling even with seq.

children.label: std::terminate
children.note: An exception escaping an element access function terminates under every standard policy.

children.label: bad_alloc
children.note: Thrown by the algorithm itself if it cannot get temporary memory.

children.label: No exception_list
children.note: The Parallelism TS design was not adopted into C++17.

children.label: reduce vs accumulate
children.note: A generalized sum may regroup and reorder; a left fold may not.

children.label: Associative and commutative
children.note: reduce and transform_reduce give the fold's result only for such operations.

children.label: Scans
children.note: inclusive_scan and exclusive_scan may regroup but keep order: associative is enough.

children.label: Floating point
children.note: Parallel or unrolled float sums differ between libraries and runs; all are valid.

children.label: init type
children.note: The accumulator has init's type, so 0 over doubles truncates.

children.label: transform_reduce
children.note: Fuses map and reduce; the two-range form is the parallel inner_product.

children.label: Requirements and gaps
children.note: Policy overloads need forward iterators and do not exist for every algorithm.

children.label: Forward iterators
children.note: Required even where the serial overload takes input iterators; not diagnosed by GCC.

children.label: No policy overload
children.note: accumulate, partial_sum, iota, binary searches, heap ops, permutations, ranges.

children.label: Implementations
children.note: Permission is not parallelism: measure on your toolchain.

children.label: libstdc++
children.note: Uses TBB if <tbb/tbb.h> is found, needing -ltbb; otherwise silently serial.

children.label: libc++
children.note: Needs -fexperimental-library; libdispatch on macOS; only a subset of overloads.

children.label: Small inputs
children.note: Task startup and the final combine can make par slower than a plain loop.
